subject: Request: Price-stitch approval for Orbis Health 36m (renewal protection ask)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orbis 36m - price stitch & renewal protection (requesting exec review)

Team —

Summary: Orbis Health (large payer prospect) has pushed for a 36‑month commitment with a blended 40% discount vs list in year 1, stepping to a small uplift in years 2–3. They insist on a renewal-protection clause (cap uplift to max +10% at renewal and a price-stitch escape for material regulatory change). This is outside standard Deal Desk guardrails and exceeds standard uplift caps.

Why: Orbis is 2nd largest regional payer in their footprint; winning this deal is materially strategic for our payer vertical motion and could open 3 integration pilots (claims routing, embedding).

What I'm asking: Exec approval to accept the proposed commercial construct with the following guardrails:
- 36‑month term; 40% effective discount Year 1 (blended).
- Renewal protection: capped uplift <= 10% on renewal (absolute cap on list-based pricing).
- Price-stitch clause: allow customers to request a limited repricing if new regulation reduces unit economics; any execution triggers require 30d notice and Deal Desk signoff.
- One-time onboarding credit of $75k in Q1 to offset integration costs (non-recurring).

Attached: Orbis_Proposal_v3.pdf (commercial schedule + usage forecast).

Risks: short-term unit economics compression; precedent if we accept broad regulatory escape language without strict trigger definition.

I've redlined the term sheet (term_sheet_price_stitch.docx) with suggested legal language — legal has flagged the escape clause as high risk, recommends narrow objective triggers only.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao

+1 on the ask — forwarding to Marissa for exec clearance. A couple quick clarifications before we escalate:
- Confirm ACV profile by year (Aditya: the attached forecast shows a sharp step-down in year 2 usage assumptions; please confirm sensitivity).
- Can we narrow the price-stitch triggers to: (a) legislative requirement that materially increases per-token compute costs, (b) forced data residency change requiring private deployment that increases per-token cost by >15%? Legal prefers objective triggers.

If Marissa greenlights with the guardrails above, recommend we: (1) approve onboarding credit $75k capped to integration milestones, (2) require standard auto-fallback to a higher-capacity model family if usage exceeds forecasts (protects runtime economics).

Marissa —

Looping you in for a decision on the non-standard commercial asks from Orbis. Highlights: 36m term, 40% first-year blended discount, 10% renewal uplift cap, price-stitch clause (as drafted it's broad). Deal Desk recommends conditional approval if exec signs off on the following constraints:

1) Narrow price-stitch to objective / binary triggers (see Jon's note).
2) Onboarding credit staged to milestones (50% on kick, 50% on production).
3) Contract to include automatic model family fallback and usage band pricing for >120% of forecast.
4) Requires Legal to sign off final clause language; Procurement to accept no retroactive credits.

This is time sensitive — Orbis asked for final terms by COB Tuesday 10/05. If Marissa approves, I'll instruct Deal Desk to prepare the final term sheet and DocuSign envelope.

Subject: Re: Orbis 36m - price stitch & renewal protection (requesting exec review)

Team —

I reviewed the ask and the redlines. Given strategic value and the potential to scale in the payer vertical, I approve proceeding with the commercial construct under the following firm conditions (no exceptions):

1) Price-stitch limited to two objective triggers only: (A) new statutory/regulatory requirement that increases per-unit compute or compliance cost by >20% (with independent third-party cost validation), (B) mandatory customer data residency migration requiring architecture change that increases OPEX by >15%.
2) Renewal uplift capped at <=10% (absolute) and subject to our published model catalog list price reference.
3) Onboarding credit $75k, payable 50% on kick + 50% on production acceptance; credit subject to clawback if customer churns within 12 months.
4) Legal to finalize wording and attach an explicit examples appendix to avoid ambiguous language.
5) Deal Desk to add automatic model fallback and over-usage banding (pricing steps) to protect economics.

Kimberly — please prepare final term sheet with these conditions. Aditya — once you have customer signoff, send to DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/signed/abcd1234 and copy legal.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Global Sales | Redwood Inference
